**THE OPPORTUNITY

**At Boozt, we are rethinking how we connect with our customers through data, personalisation, automation and AI. As our CRM setup continues to evolve, we are looking for a Marketing Automation Specialist who wants to help shape the next chapter.

This is an opportunity to take an active role in developing how we work with marketing automation at Boozt. You will join a team with ambitions to make our communication smarter, more relevant and more data-driven, with room to challenge existing approaches and explore how new technology can improve the way we work.

If you enjoy combining technical expertise with curiosity and a drive to make things better, this is your chance to make a real impact on how we do CRM at Boozt.

**What You Will Do

**You will be part of our CRM team, working hands-on with Salesforce Marketing Cloud to build and manage automated communications across email, app push and SMS. You will work closely with customer data to set up segmentation and personalisation, design targeted communications and continuously improve how we reach our customers.

**Your Main Responsibilities Will Include

**

• 
Build and manage automated communications and recurring campaigns in Salesforce Marketing Cloud (SFMC).

• 
Set up audience segmentation and personalisation using customer data, including SQL and AMPscript where relevant.

• 
Design and build personalised communications across email, app push and SMS.

• 
Analyse campaign performance, run A/B tests and use insights to improve results.

• 
Work closely with the CRM and market teams to ensure relevant communication across markets.

• 
Explore how AI and automation can improve the way we build, personalise and optimise customer communications.

**YOUR PROFILE

**You have hands-on experience with marketing automation and enjoy combining technical execution with analytical thinking and a curiosity for what is possible. You take ownership of your work, look for ways to improve and are comfortable exploring new approaches.

**We Imagine That You Bring

**

• 
Around 3 years of experience with marketing automation, preferably within CRM.

• 
Experience with a platform such as Salesforce Marketing Cloud, Braze, Adobe, Agillic, Voyado, Bloomreach or Klaviyo.

• 
A solid understanding of segmentation, personalisation, automated journeys and campaign testing.

• 
Experience working with campaign KPIs and using data to improve performance.

• 
An interest in AI tools such as ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini and how they can support your daily work.

• 
Strong written communication skills and fluency in English.

Experience with SQL and AMPscript, as well as working across multiple markets, is a plus.

**WHY BOOZT

**At Boozt, you will join a fast-paced and ambitious environment where you have the freedom and responsibility to make a real impact. As part of our CRM team, you will work at the intersection of customer experience, data, technology and commercial growth. This approximately 14-month maternity cover is an opportunity to take ownership, explore new ideas and help shape the customer experience for millions of customers while developing your skills in e-commerce CRM.

**Apply today – we’re excited to learn more about you!

_Only applications submitted in English will be considered.

_Important: Applicants must have the legal right to work in Denmark at the time of employment. Please note that this position does not include visa sponsorship or relocation support.

We review applications on an ongoing basis. You can read more about the process under **Recruitment.

****BOOZT PERKS

**

• 
Great personal and internal career development opportunities

• 
A culture built on our values of trust, freedom, and responsibility

• 
Driven and passionate international colleagues

• 
A generous employee discount

• 
Healthy and delicious breakfast and lunch, top-quality coffee, and fresh fruit available all day

• 
In-house gym, onsite masseuse, and medical doctor

• 
An amazing HQ in central Copenhagen – the iconic, energy-efficient Krystallen building, recognized for its architectural design and sustainability. Enjoy breathtaking city views and much more!

The IT University of Copenhagen invites highly motivated individuals to apply for a Postdoc position starting in January or soon thereafter.

We invite applicants who want to contribute to the IT University's vision of creating and sharing knowledge that is profound and leads to ground-breaking information technology and services for the benefit of humanity.

**Job Description

**The postdoc will work with the Horizon-funded FEMVision project, which targets online visual misogyny. The project studies how misogyny circulates through images and memes in everyday digital spaces. The candidate will participate in the project's computational analysis, including fine-tuning and validating a multimodal large language model classifier for visual misogyny, benchmarked against expert human coders. Building on this classifier, the Postdoc will conduct semantic clustering of the visual corpus to map the iconographic and thematic repertoires of online misogyny, and analyze how users react to and negotiate misogynistic content across platforms.

The ideal candidate has experience with computational social science methods and has worked with using LLMs for complex data annotation and validation. Experience with social media data collection and working within the Meta Content Library is a plus.

You will work closely with Associate Professor Luca Rossi, PI at ITU.

**General information

**The IT University of Copenhagen (ITU) is a teaching and research-based university specializing in information technology (IT) and the opportunities it offers. The IT University has more than 160 full-time Faculty members. Research and teaching in information technology span all academic activities which involve computers including computer science, information and media sciences, humanities and social sciences, business impact and the commercialization of IT.

**Research at the IT University of Copenhagen

**Our research is organized through dynamic research groups, centers, hubs, and labs that promote collaboration across disciplines. These units explore complex challenges at the intersection of people, technology, and society, contributing both to fundamental insights and practical solutions. At ITU, we see research as a shared endeavor – open, critically engaged, and rooted in dialogue with academic communities, industry, and the public sector. We actively pursue international partnerships and networks, and our interdisciplinary approach ensures that our research not only advances knowledge but also generates impact beyond academia.

**Teaching at the IT University of Copenhagen

**ITU currently offers four BSc degrees, six MSc degrees and one professional master’s degree, spanning across these disciplines. ITU's education is extremely sought after and produces qualified graduates who are in high demand from the job market.

**Working at the IT University

**Located in modern architecture, a 6-minute metro ride from the center of Copenhagen, the IT University offers an informal working environment, a varied everyday life, and a highly motivated, innovative, skilled, and diverse international faculty, with PhD degrees from more than 20 different countries. The IT University is an equal opportunity employer and prides itself in actively pursuing an improved gender balance among students and among faculty.

**Working in Copenhagen

**Copenhagen has a solid educational system, a rich cultural life, universal healthcare, good childcare, and well-functioning infrastructure. Copenhagen is consistently ranked among the world’s most livable cities according to the Economist Global Liveability Index. Living and working in Copenhagen will typically be a great experience for you and your family.

**Salary and terms of employment

**Appointment and salary will be in accordance with the Ministry of Taxation’s agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC) and job structure for academic staff at universities.

**Qualification Requirements

**The following qualifications are required:

• Candidates are required to have academic qualifications at PhD level

**Application

**The application and all other documents ought to be in English and must include:

• A motivated application (cover letter), including a detailed description of your qualifications and brief statements of research and teaching plans

• A full CV, including name, address, phone number, e-mail, previous and present employment and academic background

• Documentation of academic degrees (copy of degree certificates etc.)

• Relevant scientific publications or/and PhD thesis written by the applicant

• Documentation of pedagogical experience and teaching record within one or more of the teaching areas listed for the position

Applications without the above-mentioned required documents will not be assessed.

The applicant will be assessed according to the Appointment Order from the Ministry of ScienceTechnology and Innovation of 13 March 2012.

The IT University may use shortlisting in connection with the recruitment process. In case of shortlisting, the Chair of the hiring committee selects applicants for assessment in consultation with the hiring committee after the application deadline. All applicants are notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The shortlisting of candidates for assessment is based on the criteria in the job posting.

**Further information

**Questions about the positions can be directed to Associate Professor, Luca Rossi, IT University of Copenhagen, lucr@itu.dk or tel. +4572185036.

Questions related to the application procedure may be directed to HR, hr@itu.dk.

**Application procedure

**You can only apply for this position through our e-recruitment system. Apply by pressing the button "Apply for position" in the job announcement on our website .

The IT University might upon request in the interview process contact 1-2 references.

Application deadline: **30 October 2026, at 23:59 CET/CEST.

**Applications/enclosures received at ITU after the application deadline will not be taken into consideration. If you submit an application, it is your responsibility to ensure that it arrives before the deadline so please allow sufficient time for upload of publications and other documents.

At The IT University of Copenhagen, we have an international environment and view diversity as a valuable resource. We are committed to ensuring an inclusive working environment for all our employees and encourage all qualified applicants, regardless of age, gender, religious affiliation, or ethnic background to apply for the position.

As ITU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Do you want to create lasting value for communities while helping shape Denmark's fossil-free future?

We are looking for an experienced and strategic Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager to play a leading role in the development of the Hesselø offshore wind project, one of Denmark's most significant future renewable energy projects.

The Hesselø offshore wind project is located in the Kattegat Sea between Denmark and Sweden, approximately 30 kilometres from the coast, with a minimum installed capacity of 800 MW. The project includes both offshore and onshore infrastructure and will make a significant contribution to Denmark's future fossil-free energy production.

As Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager, you will help ensure that the project is developed in close collaboration with local communities, stakeholders and partners. You will lead stakeholder engagement activities throughout the development process, helping create understanding, trust and meaningful dialogue while supporting the successful delivery of this strategically important infrastructure project.

You will act as one of the project's key representatives and serve as a bridge between the project organisation and external stakeholders, ensuring that local insights, concerns and opportunities are incorporated into decision-making processes.

Working closely with colleagues across Consenting, Communications, Public & Regulatory Affairs, Development, Environmental functions and Project Delivery, you will help shape how Vattenfall engages with communities, authorities and stakeholders throughout the project's lifecycle.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

What will you do?

As Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager, you will design and implement stakeholder engagement and communication strategies that support project development, permitting and long-term success. This includes mapping and analysing stakeholder interests, developing engagement plans and ensuring that activities meet regulatory requirements while going beyond compliance.

You will build and maintain trusted relationships with communities, municipalities, authorities, NGOs, industry organisations, businesses, landowners and other stakeholders. As a key point of contact, you will facilitate constructive dialogue, capture feedback and ensure that local insights are reflected in project decision-making.

You will also create clear content for project channels and public meetings, provide transparent and timely information, and strengthen local understanding of offshore wind. Working closely with Public & Regulatory Affairs, Communications, Environmental teams and Project Delivery, Yyou will identify opportunities to maximise local value creation and positive social impact.

Your responsibilities will include:

Stakeholder Engagement & Consultation

• Design and deliver consultation activities and public participation processes throughout the project lifecycle.

• Act as the primary point of contact for local communities, interest groups and key stakeholders. Facilitating constructive dialogue and good neighbourship, creating understanding and trust between projects and local communities.

• Build trusted relationships and ensure stakeholder feedback is effectively integrated into project decision-making.

• Deliver meaningful stakeholder involvement that meets regulatory requirements and supports Vattenfall's ambition to go beyond compliance; identifying and supporting opportunities for local value creation.

Communications & Community Relations

• Ensure communities and stakeholders receive transparent, accurate and timely information throughout project development and delivery.

• Identify and support initiatives that enhance local value creation, community benefits and understanding of offshore wind.

Cross-functional Collaboration

• Represent Vattenfall at stakeholder forums, public events and consultation meetings, while supporting alignment across Hesselø, other Danish developments and the operational offshore wind portfolio.

• Contribute to supplier, local supply chain and landowner engagement activities where required.

• You will work in alignment and collaboration with the wider (Danish) Stakeholder Engagement team and their activities towards our development and operational portfolio.

Who are you?

You are an experienced stakeholder engagement professional who enjoys building relationships, creating trust and finding solutions in complex environments. With at least five years of relevant experience from major infrastructure, renewable energy or sustainable development projects, you understand that successful projects depend as much on people and communities as on technology and engineering. You have worked with external stakeholders such as communities, municipalities, NGOs, businesses and landowners, and you are confident developing engagement programmes, communication strategies and clear content for different audiences. You combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution and are comfortable navigating multiple interests, perspectives and priorities across development, permitting, construction or operational phases. As a natural relationship builder, you communicate clearly, listen attentively and remain calm and constructive in sensitive discussions. You are structured, proactive and collaborative, and motivated by the opportunity to contribute to the energy transition while creating positive outcomes for communities and society.

Next to this, you bring:

• A university degree in Communications, Community Development, Psychology, International Development, Political Science, Social Sciences or a related discipline.

• At least five years of experience in stakeholder engagement, community relations, communications or public consultation within major infrastructure, renewable energy or sustainable development projects.

• Strong understanding of stakeholder engagement across project development, permitting, construction or operational phases.

• Strong relationship-building, facilitation, influencing and conflict-resolution skills.

• Excellent Danish and English language skills, both written and spoken.

• Experience from offshore wind, renewable energy or major infrastructure projects is an advantage, particularly involving permitting or consenting processes or engagement with marine users, fisheries, environmental organisations, coastal communities, regulatory bodies or political stakeholders.

Location

Copenhagen or Kolding (DK). Frequent travel to project-relevant locations and occasional international travel required. You will be part of an international team.

Additional Information

Our offer

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can really find your element with us. We’ll also provide you with all the learning and development you need to expand your horizons.

We strive to be the best place to work in the industry with highly competitive pay and conditions and an open, supportive culture. A commitment to a healthy work-life balance aims to ensure everyone plays to their strengths, whatever their background and experiences.

You will be part of a growing team of 1,700+ colleagues from 50+ nationalities where our positive approach to diversity is reflected in the fact that more than a quarter of staff are women.

More Information

For more information about the position or recruitment process you are welcome to contact our recruiter Christian Pathuel, christian.pathuel@vattenfall.com

We welcome your application in English no later than 28th of October 2026. We kindly request that you do not send applications by any means other than via our website.

Vattenfall works actively for all employees to have the same opportunities and rights regardless of gender, ethnicity, age, transgender identity or expression, religion or other belief, disability or sexual orientation. Click here for further information.

The security of Vattenfall and its employees is essential. For that reason, a pre-employment screening will be part of your recruitment process. The screening is based on the role you will fulfill within Vattenfall and will be performed by a third party, DISA Global Solutions AB.

jobs.description:
Company Description

Vattenfall is a leading European energy company driving the transition to a sustainable energy system. We have been electrifying industries, powering homes and transforming life through innovation for more than 100 years. We employ around 21 000 people mostly in our core markets in Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, Denmark, and the UK.

Job Description

Do you want to create lasting value for communities while helping shape Denmark's fossil-free future?

We are looking for an experienced and strategic Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager to play a leading role in the development of the Hesselø offshore wind project, one of Denmark's most significant future renewable energy projects.

The Hesselø offshore wind project is located in the Kattegat Sea between Denmark and Sweden, approximately 30 kilometres from the coast, with a minimum installed capacity of 800 MW. The project includes both offshore and onshore infrastructure and will make a significant contribution to Denmark's future fossil-free energy production.

As Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager, you will help ensure that the project is developed in close collaboration with local communities, stakeholders and partners. You will lead stakeholder engagement activities throughout the development process, helping create understanding, trust and meaningful dialogue while supporting the successful delivery of this strategically important infrastructure project.

You will act as one of the project's key representatives and serve as a bridge between the project organisation and external stakeholders, ensuring that local insights, concerns and opportunities are incorporated into decision-making processes.

Working closely with colleagues across Consenting, Communications, Public & Regulatory Affairs, Development, Environmental functions and Project Delivery, you will help shape how Vattenfall engages with communities, authorities and stakeholders throughout the project's lifecycle.

Be in your element with BA Wind

As part of BA Wind you will play a key role in one of the most exciting pipelines in the industry with 24GW of capacity stretching out more than a decade ahead across our key European markets.

You won’t only be involved in developing projects but pioneering cutting-edge innovation, new business models and ways of working with communities and the environment. Working as part of a leading European utility also means you could be helping a growing number of major businesses and brands achieve their own sustainability goals through partnerships.

Qualifications

What will you do?

As Senior Stakeholder Engagement Manager, you will design and implement stakeholder engagement and communication strategies that support project development, permitting and long-term success. This includes mapping and analysing stakeholder interests, developing engagement plans and ensuring that activities meet regulatory requirements while going beyond compliance.

You will build and maintain trusted relationships with communities, municipalities, authorities, NGOs, industry organisations, businesses, landowners and other stakeholders. As a key point of contact, you will facilitate constructive dialogue, capture feedback and ensure that local insights are reflected in project decision-making.

You will also create clear content for project channels and public meetings, provide transparent and timely information, and strengthen local understanding of offshore wind. Working closely with Public & Regulatory Affairs, Communications, Environmental teams and Project Delivery, Yyou will identify opportunities to maximise local value creation and positive social impact.

Your responsibilities will include:

Stakeholder Engagement & Consultation

• Design and deliver consultation activities and public participation processes throughout the project lifecycle.

• Act as the primary point of contact for local communities, interest groups and key stakeholders. Facilitating constructive dialogue and good neighbourship, creating understanding and trust between projects and local communities.

• Build trusted relationships and ensure stakeholder feedback is effectively integrated into project decision-making.

• Deliver meaningful stakeholder involvement that meets regulatory requirements and supports Vattenfall's ambition to go beyond compliance; identifying and supporting opportunities for local value creation.

Communications & Community Relations

• Ensure communities and stakeholders receive transparent, accurate and timely information throughout project development and delivery.

• Identify and support initiatives that enhance local value creation, community benefits and understanding of offshore wind.

Cross-functional Collaboration

• Represent Vattenfall at stakeholder forums, public events and consultation meetings, while supporting alignment across Hesselø, other Danish developments and the operational offshore wind portfolio.

• Contribute to supplier, local supply chain and landowner engagement activities where required.

Who are you?

You are an experienced stakeholder engagement professional who enjoys building relationships, creating trust and finding solutions in complex environments. With at least five years of relevant experience from major infrastructure, renewable energy or sustainable development projects, you understand that successful projects depend as much on people and communities as on technology and engineering. You have worked with external stakeholders such as communities, municipalities, NGOs, businesses and landowners, and you are confident developing engagement programmes, communication strategies and clear content for different audiences. You combine strategic thinking with hands-on execution and are comfortable navigating multiple interests, perspectives and priorities across development, permitting, construction or operational phases. As a natural relationship builder, you communicate clearly, listen attentively and remain calm and constructive in sensitive discussions. You are structured, proactive and collaborative, and motivated by the opportunity to contribute to the energy transition while creating positive outcomes for communities and society.

Next to this, you bring:

• At least five years of experience in stakeholder engagement, community relations, communications or public consultation within major infrastructure, renewable energy or sustainable development projects.

• Strong understanding of stakeholder engagement across project development, permitting, construction or operational phases.

Location

Copenhagen or Kolding (DK). Frequent travel to project-relevant locations and occasional international travel required. You will be part of an international team.

Additional Information

Looking for a career with growth?

Looking for a role where your superpowers can be leveraged to the maximum and with limitless opportunities for growth?

The scale and ambition of our wind, battery and solar business means you can really find your element with us. We’ll also provide you with all the learning and development you need to expand your horizons.

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is an advanced systems and industrialization company developing integrated technology platforms for demanding aerospace, security, and mission-critical applications. Its mission is to transform operationally validated technologies into scalable, ready-to-deploy systems by combining advanced engineering, industrial partnerships, and strong governance.

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development. The site will build core capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, industrialization, and deployment of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be an advanced aerospace signal-intelligence product platform covering RF and system architecture, antenna-system design, RF and microwave hardware, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for qualification, production, and operational deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and international deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s mechanical design capability for antenna and RF systems. The role is intended for an experienced mechanical engineer with prior hands-on experience developing the mechanical implementation of antenna, RF, or microwave hardware.

You will design and develop mechanical solutions for antenna systems and associated RF and electronic assemblies. The work includes antenna supports and mounts, RF-aware enclosures, radomes, fixed and, where applicable, deployable antenna mechanisms, test fixtures, thermal solutions, connector integration, cable routing, sealing, environmental protection, and platform interfaces. Many of these structures can directly affect antenna and RF performance, requiring close co-design with antenna and RF engineers.

The role covers mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing-process selection, structural and thermal analysis, tolerance definition, detailed CAD design, prototyping, assembly, environmental validation, serviceability, and production release. Particular attention will be given to mechanical structures that directly affect antenna performance, integration, alignment, stability, and deployment.

You will work closely with antenna systems engineers, RF and microwave hardware engineers, system architects, RF test and characterization engineers, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams. The role requires strong mechanical design expertise, RF-aware product thinking, end-to-end technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototype build and qualification to documented, manufacturable antenna assemblies and integrated systems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system, antenna, and platform requirements into mechanical architectures, interface definitions, design constraints, and technical trade-offs.

• Design mechanical components and assemblies for antenna systems, including supports, mounts, frames, radomes, RF-aware enclosures, fixed or deployable mechanisms, and platform-integration structures.

• Own the detailed mechanical implementation of antenna and RF assemblies, including 3D CAD models, 2D manufacturing drawings, GD&T, assembly-level tolerance analysis, BOMs, and configuration-controlled documentation.

• Develop mechanical solutions that maintain antenna alignment, dimensional stability, RF clearances, grounding, shielding, cable routing, connector accessibility, and other mechanical conditions required to achieve the intended electromagnetic performance.

• Integrate RF modules, antennas, electronics, connectors, cables, gaskets, thermal interfaces, and environmental sealing into complete mechanical assemblies.

• Perform structural, thermal, and tolerance analyses covering stiffness, strength, mass properties, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, and expected environmental loads.

• Define mechanical requirements and work jointly with antenna and RF engineers to establish electromagnetic constraints for radomes, covers, supports, enclosures, and other structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Design antenna deployment and positioning mechanisms, where applicable, including hinges, latches, restraints, stops, alignment features, and associated interfaces.

• Design test fixtures, alignment tools, handling aids, assembly tooling, and prototype-support hardware for antenna and RF system development.

• Select materials, coatings, surface treatments, fasteners, adhesives, seals, bearings, and manufacturing processes based on structural, thermal, RF, environmental, corrosion, and production requirements.

• Lead mechanical prototype build, assembly, troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Contribute to environmental testing and qualification, including vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, and other relevant mechanical validation activities.

• Apply design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly, serviceability, reliability, and cost considerations throughout development.

• Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners on technical clarification, process selection, prototype production, inspection, non-conformance resolution, and production release.

• Prepare mechanical specifications, analysis reports, interface-control documentation, design-review materials, assembly instructions, and production handover documentation.

• Collaborate with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and engineering workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Required qualifications and experience

• Degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

• 5+ years of professional mechanical design experience, including demonstrated experience developing mechanical hardware for antenna, RF, or microwave systems where mechanical geometry, materials, interfaces, tolerances, or nearby structures directly influence electromagnetic performance.

• Strong hands-on experience and demonstrated technical ownership of complex mechanical assemblies from initial architecture and concept through detailed design, prototype build, verification, qualification, and production release.

• Advanced proficiency with a professional 3D CAD and drafting environment; SolidWorks experience is preferred.

• Strong command of GD&T, engineering drawing standards, assembly-level tolerance analysis, and production-quality mechanical documentation.

• Demonstrated experience designing mechanical components or assemblies for antenna, RF, or microwave systems, such as antenna supports and mounts, frames, enclosures, radomes, mechanisms, fixtures, or other mechanically and electromagnetically constrained structures.

• Experience with mechanical packaging and integration of antennas, RF modules, PCBs, connectors, cables, thermal interfaces, shielding, grounding, seals, and associated electronics.

• Practical understanding of RF-aware mechanical design, including the effects of materials, structures, clearances, alignment, grounding, shielding, cabling, and radomes on antenna and RF performance.

• Experience applying engineering calculations and simulation methods, including finite-element analysis where appropriate, to support structural and thermal design decisions.

• Understanding of stiffness, strength, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, fatigue, and other relevant environmental loads.

• Practical knowledge of metallic materials, engineering polymers, elastomers, composites, adhesives, coatings, and surface treatments.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, such as precision machining, sheet-metal fabrication, additive manufacturing, composite manufacturing, joining, fastening, sealing, and assembly.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with prototype assembly, mechanical troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Experience supporting environmental testing and qualification, such as vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, or comparable validation activities.

• Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing teams on process selection, technical clarification, inspection, non-conformance resolution, manufacturability, and production handover.

Nice to have

• Experience developing lightweight, stiffness-critical structures with stringent alignment and dimensional-stability requirements.

• Experience with aerospace or space-hardware qualification, including thermal-vacuum testing, outgassing constraints, vibration, and shock.

• Experience with precision mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, antenna positioning, and calibration or verification fixtures.

• Experience designing IP-rated enclosures or ruggedized outdoor electronic equipment.

• Experience with product data management, configuration control, and release processes for complex mechanical assemblies.

• Experience working with international suppliers and manufacturing partners on low-volume, high-complexity hardware.

• Experience designing radomes, RF-transparent structures, or mechanical structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Experience with mechanically steerable, deployable, foldable, or position-critical antenna systems.

• Experience working directly with antenna or electromagnetic simulation engineers to iterate mechanical geometry, materials, and interfaces based on RF performance.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take end-to-end technical ownership of one or more mechanical subsystems or integration areas for antenna and RF systems.

• Establish the initial mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing approach, and platform-integration plan for the assigned scope.

• Deliver reviewed 3D models, manufacturing drawings, tolerance analyses, interface definitions, and supporting design documentation.

• Develop and support the build, assembly, and verification of initial mechanical prototypes, fixtures, or engineering models.

• Identify key structural, thermal, alignment, sealing, deployment, and manufacturability risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, supplier, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and release workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Shape the future of education technology

At IST, we're building the cloud platform that powers educational solutions used by more than five million users across Europe. Unlike most cloud teams, we run our own cloud — on our own hardware, in our own data center. That means the abstraction stops with us: when a node misbehaves, there's no support ticket to a hyperscaler.

There's a rack, and someone who knows it.

We're looking for a Cloud Engineer who finds that appealing rather than daunting.

About the role

As a Cloud Engineer, you'll help design, build and operate the IST Cloud Platform — from the automation and orchestration layers our developers build on, all the way down to the switches, servers and cabling that carry it. You'll do this together with our Cloud Engineering team, architects, developers and stakeholders, whether the work happens at a keyboard or in a rack.

In practice, around a quarter of your time will be spent physically on site in the data center. Not as a separate duty, but as a natural part of the work: expanding capacity for a new cluster the team has just automated, replacing a switch that's been throwing errors in your own monitoring, tracing a network issue that turns out to be a cable rather than a config. Owning the platform end to end is what makes this role different from a pure cloud position.

The role is based at our office in Roskilde, Denmark, with the primary data center within reach. Some travel is required, primarily to our office in Växjö, Sweden.

Just as importantly, you're comfortable at both ends of the stack. You can discuss platform architecture with our developers in the morning and spend the afternoon in the rack with a screwdriver, and you see those as the same job rather than two different ones. What we offer

This is a full-time, permanent position. We apply an office-first policy, and given the hands-on nature of this role, regular physical presence at the office and in the datacenter is part of the job. Within that framework, there's room for flexibility on the days where your work doesn't require you on site.

You'll join an international and collaborative environment where you'll have real ownership, influence over strategic technology decisions, and the chance to help shape the future of learning.

jobs.description:
Recent advances in machine learning and deep learning are opening new possibilities for computational imaging, including the reconstruction of complex 3D structures from experimental imaging data. In this fully funded PhD project at DTU Compute, you will develop novel learning-based methods for X-ray nano-tomography. As state-of-the-art synchrotron imaging systems push towards ever higher spatial resolution, even minute positioning errors, mechanical drift, and sample deformations become sources of image degradation. The central challenge is to reconstruct accurate 3D and 4D representations of samples while accounting for positional uncertainties during image acquisition and changes in sample shape over time.

The project will bring together neural representations, inverse problems, geometric modeling, and computational imaging to address fundamental challenges in nano-tomography. Rather than correcting acquisition errors and sample deformations as separate preprocessing steps, you will investigate how to model and estimate the sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation jointly from the measured data.

The position is based at DTU Compute and conducted in close collaboration with EPFL and the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI) in Switzerland, one of the leading centers for synchrotron X-ray imaging. As a PhD student, you will work in an international research environment spanning DTU, EPFL, and PSI, combining expertise in both machine learning and computational imaging with access to experimental data and advanced imaging facilities. Research visits to Switzerland are planned as part of the project.

Responsibilities

• Develop novel machine learning and deep learning methods for X-ray nano-tomography, which jointly reconstruct sample structure, acquisition geometry, and deformation fields from inconsistent projection data.
• Investigate neural field representations for 3D and 4D imaging, including models that capture changes in sample geometry over time, and explore hybrid approaches combining learning-based methods with physical models of image formation and tomographic reconstruction.
• Validate and evaluate the developed methods using experimental nano-tomography data, initially focusing on integrated circuits.
• Collaborate with researchers at DTU, PSI, and EPFL, and participate in international research visits and scientific activities.
• Publish research results in leading journals and conferences in machine learning, computer vision, and computational imaging.
• Contribute to research-based teaching and supervision of MSc and BSc student projects.
• Participate in activities within the Center for Quantification of Imaging Data from MAX IV (QIM), including workshops, training courses, and interdisciplinary research collaborations.
Qualifications
You are curious and motivated by developing new machine learning methods to solve challenging problems in computational imaging. A strong background in machine learning and deep learning is particularly important. We welcome candidates from computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, and related disciplines who are interested in combining modern learning methods with mathematical modeling and real-world experimental data. The candidate should be able to work independently, contribute effectively to an interdisciplinary research team, and communicate scientific ideas clearly in written and spoken English.

To succeed in this position, you are expected to have:

• A master's degree in computer science, applied mathematics, physics, engineering, or a related discipline.
• A strong background in machine learning and deep learning, including experience developing, implementing, or evaluating learning-based models.
• Experience with scientific programming, preferably in Python, and familiarity with relevant machine learning frameworks.
• A solid understanding of mathematical modeling, optimization, or numerical methods.
Experience in one or more of the following areas is an advantage:

• Neural representations, implicit neural fields, or other coordinate-based representations.

• Inverse problems, image reconstruction, or physics-informed machine learning.
• Image registration, motion estimation, or deformable modeling.
• Image processing, image analysis, or tomographic reconstruction.
